title: Lagna and the first house
text: In Jyotisha, the Lagna and first house are commonly used as a starting point for discussing temperament, the way a person approaches life, and embodied presence. A sign placement supplies the chart's calculated frame; interpretation describes traditional symbolism, not a guaranteed personality or outcome.
source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra, Ch. 4 (Lagna considerations)

title: Moon and emotional habits
text: The Moon is traditionally considered in relation to the mind, perception, habits, and emotional responsiveness. Its calculated sign and house can be discussed as symbolic tendencies and needs; they do not establish a diagnosis or determine a person's feelings.
source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra, planetary significations

title: Sun and agency
text: Traditional Jyotisha associates the Sun with vitality, authority, purpose, and self-direction. Interpretations should connect these themes to the Sun's supplied sign or house without inventing dignity, aspects, conjunctions, or life events.
source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra, planetary significations

title: Mars and initiative
text: Mars is traditionally discussed through courage, initiative, energy, competition, and conflict. A chart reading may use its verified sign and house as prompts for reflection on action and assertion, without treating symbolism as a certain prediction.
source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra, planetary significations

title: Mercury and learning
text: Mercury is traditionally associated with speech, reasoning, trade, calculation, and learning. Its chart placement can frame a discussion of communication and study preferences, while avoiding unsupported claims about specific abilities or outcomes.
source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra, planetary significations

title: Jupiter and guidance
text: Jupiter is traditionally linked with knowledge, counsel, ethics, growth, and teachers. This symbolism can be related to a verified placement as a reflective theme; it does not guarantee wealth, success, or moral character.
source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra, planetary significations

title: Venus and relating
text: Venus is traditionally considered for affection, pleasure, art, harmony, and comforts. Its supplied placement can support a careful discussion of relational preferences and values, without making a definitive claim about marriage or a partner.
source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra, planetary significations

title: Saturn and sustained effort
text: Saturn is traditionally associated with time, discipline, responsibility, endurance, and limits. A verified house and sign may be used to discuss areas where patience and structure are emphasized; this is not a prediction of hardship.
source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra, planetary significations

title: Fourth house and home
text: The fourth house is traditionally considered for home, roots, inner contentment, and foundational education. Readings should state which supplied planets occupy it and distinguish symbolic associations from facts about a person's family or property.
source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra, house significations

title: Fifth house and study
text: The fifth house is traditionally discussed in relation to learning, creativity, discernment, and children. Its occupants may be described only from calculated chart data; interpretation should not promise academic results or fertility outcomes.
source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra, house significations

title: Seventh house and partnership
text: The seventh house is traditionally used when discussing partnership, agreements, and one-to-one relationships. These associations can invite reflection on cooperation and expectations, but cannot establish whether or when someone will marry.
source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra, house significations

title: Tenth house and vocation
text: The tenth house is traditionally considered for action in the world, responsibilities, vocation, and public contribution. It can frame discussion of working style from supplied placements, without asserting a particular career or guaranteed status.
source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra, house significations

title: Second house and resources
text: The second house is traditionally associated with accumulated resources, speech, food, and family lineage. These are interpretive themes rather than financial advice or evidence of a person's actual assets.
source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra, house significations

title: Eleventh house and gains
text: The eleventh house is traditionally considered for gains, networks, aspirations, and supportive communities. Its symbolism can be discussed as a prompt about goals and group connections; it does not predict income.
source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra, house significations

title: Vimshottari dasha periods
text: Vimshottari dasha is a traditional planetary-period framework. The supplied period names and dates are chart data; general interpretations describe themes associated with the period lord and must not be used to claim a certain event or timing.
source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra, Vimshottari Dasha system

title: Signs as interpretive context
text: A zodiac sign provides a traditional style or mode for interpreting a planet or house. The sign name must come from the calculated chart. Sign symbolism is interpretive context and should not be presented as a scientifically established personality measure.
source: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra, Rashi and Graha interpretation
